lesson.title: A neural net from scratch

primer.title: A neuron holds a number
primer.body: Each neuron holds a number between 0 and 1, its activation. The inputs are the data; every other neuron computes its number from the layer before it.

primer.title: Weights and a bias
primer.body: Each connection multiplies the signal by a weight: positive pushes the next neuron up, negative pushes it down. The bias shifts how easily the neuron lights up.
primer.code: z = x1 * w1 + x2 * w2 + b

primer.title: Sigmoid squishes
primer.body: Sigmoid turns any total into a number between 0 and 1, so a neuron's output reads like how active it is.

primer.title: Learning goes downhill
primer.body: The loss says how wrong the outputs are. Backprop finds which way each weight should move to lower it, and each training step moves it a little that way.

lesson.overview: We'll build a neural network with nothing but NumPy and teach it XOR: output 1 when exactly one input is 1. First the network and its forward pass, then backprop, then a training loop, and last a test that prints 0 1 1 0.

build.summary: A 2-4-1 neural network in NumPy that learns XOR.
build.outcome: Run it and the loss falls below 0.001; it prints [0 1 1 0] for the four inputs.

payload.title: Write the training loop
payload.instructions: In nn.py, paste the loop under # Training
payload.details: Under # Training, add the training loop. It prints the loss every 1,000 epochs.
payload.what: A loop that steps every weight downhill 5,000 times
payload.why: Each step lowers the loss a little. The loop prints the loss every 1,000 epochs so you can watch it fall.
payload.code:
lr = 1.0
for epoch in range(5000):
    h, out = forward(X)
    dW2, db2, dW1, db1 = backward(X, y, h, out)
    W2 -= lr * dW2
    b2 -= lr * db2
    W1 -= lr * dW1
    b1 -= lr * db1
    loss = np.mean((out - y) ** 2)
    if epoch % 1000 == 0:
        print(f"epoch {epoch:4d}  loss {loss:.4f}")

payload.caption: What your loop will do: every weight takes a small step downhill 5,000 times, and ŷ settles on 0 1 1 0.

payload.title: What a neuron does
payload.body: It adds its inputs, each times a weight, plus a bias, then sigmoid squishes the total into 0..1. That number is how lit up it is.

payload.title: Sigmoid or ReLU?
payload.body: Both work. Sigmoid keeps outputs in 0..1 like XOR's answers, and its slope σ(1 − σ) keeps backprop to one line.

payload.caption: What you're building. Brightness is a neuron's activation; blue weights push up, brown push down.

payload.title: Hint 1 of 2
payload.body: Start at the output: d_out is the error times sigmoid's slope, out * (1 - out).

payload.title: How backprop assigns blame
payload.body: Start at the output: how wrong was it? Each weight into it is blamed by how much it contributed. Then do the same one layer back.

payload.title: Why out * (1 - out)?
payload.body: It's sigmoid's slope. The chain rule multiplies it in wherever the signal went through a sigmoid.

payload.caption: Backprop: the output's error flows back along the same weights, and each weight gets its share.

payload.title: Hint 1 of 2
payload.body: Copy the loop from the drawer and paste it under # Training, with its indentation.

payload.title: One pass of the loop
payload.body: forward makes a guess, backward says which way each weight should move, and each weight moves a little that way (lr sets how far). 5,000 times.

payload.title: Why lr = 1.0?
payload.body: A tiny network with a smooth loss can take big steps. On real data you'd start nearer 0.01.

payload.caption: What your loop will do: every weight takes a small step downhill 5,000 times, and ŷ settles on 0 1 1 0.

payload.title: Reading the loss
payload.body: The loss is the mean squared error over the four inputs. Answering 0.5 for everything scores 0.25; a network that has learned XOR goes below 0.01.

payload.title: Why 5,000 epochs?
payload.body: XOR needs a few thousand small steps from this start; by epoch 4000 the loss is under 0.001.

payload.title: Why zeros can't learn
payload.body: All four hidden neurons compute sigmoid(0) = 0.5 and get the same update, so they stay copies. Here the gradient is exactly zero.

payload.title: What the weights mean
payload.body: Hidden neuron 1 turns on when either input is 1 (OR); neuron 3 only when both are (AND). The output adds the first and subtracts the third: OR minus AND is XOR.

payload.title: What next?
payload.body: Swap XOR for real data: more inputs, a bigger hidden layer, and the same four pieces.
